objective.text: Keep Blade visibility checks as presentation while enforcing the same permission server-side.

difficulty.rationale: Enforce permission on the operation in addition to deciding what the interface displays.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A delete button is inside @can("delete", $post), so unauthorized users never see it. The DELETE endpoint performs no policy check. Which review finding remains valid?

options.text: The @can directive automatically installs authorization middleware on the DELETE route.
options.rationale: Rendering a conditional block does not modify the route middleware or action.
options.misconception: Rendering a conditional block does not modify the route middleware or action.

options.text: The endpoint must authorize deletion too; hiding the button does not prevent a direct request.
options.rationale: Blade controls rendered presentation, while the server endpoint must independently enforce the permission before deleting.

options.text: A CSRF token by itself proves the user may delete this particular post.
options.rationale: Request-forgery protection does not decide resource-specific deletion permission.
options.misconception: Request-forgery protection does not decide resource-specific deletion permission.

options.text: Using DELETE instead of POST makes the missing policy check unnecessary.
options.rationale: The HTTP verb does not authorize the caller for the target resource.
options.misconception: The HTTP verb does not authorize the caller for the target resource.

explanation.summary: Blade controls rendered presentation, while the server endpoint must independently enforce the permission before deleting.
